question:
A 75-year-old male presents to the emergency department with complaints of lower abdominal pain,
distension, and inability to urinate. Two days ago, he underwent knee replacement surgery, during
which a Foley catheter was placed and removed before discharge after he was able to void. The
patient reports typically waking up 4–5 times nightly to urinate but has been unable to pass urine for
over 24 hours since returning home. His medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes
mellitus, managed with lisinopril and metformin. Vital signs show a temperature of 37.2°C (100.2°F),
heart rate of 90/min, blood pressure of 159/99 mm Hg, respiratory rate of 20/min, and oxygen
saturation of 97% on room air. Physical examination reveals diffuse abdominal tenderness and
distension, with questionable right costovertebral angle tenderness. Digital rectal exam reveals a
boggy, enlarged prostate. Laboratory findings include a serum creatinine of 2.9 mg/dL (baseline 0.9
mg/dL), blood urea nitrogen of 45 mg/dL, a slightly elevated white blood cell count, and urinalysis
showing leukocytes, trace blood, and negative nitrites and leukocyte esterase. Foley catheter
placement yields minimal urine output. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
Answer Choices: (A) Administration of antibiotics for suspected urinary tract infection (B) Aggressive
intravenous fluid resuscitation (C) Repeat placement of a larger foley catheter (D) Abdominopelvic CT
scan with IV contrast (E) Emergent hemodialysis (F) Bladder scan (G) MRI of the abdomen and pelvis
to assess for structural abnormalities (H) Cystoscopy to evaluate for urethral obstruction (I) Immediate
surgical consultation for prostate resection (J) Renal ultrasound
 A. Renal ultrasound
B. Repeat placement of a larger foley catheter
C. Aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation
D. Cystoscopy to evaluate for urethral obstruction

E. Abdominopelvic CT scan with IV contrast
F. MRI of the abdomen and pelvis to assess for structural abnormalities
G. Immediate surgical consultation for prostate resection
H. Administration of antibiotics for suspected urinary tract infection
I. Bladder scan
J. Emergent hemodialysis
